spec_notes: The spec maps request sentences to five requirements and test IDs. It does not state that IllegalMoveError is an exported class (S-17), the castling-out-of/through-check rules (S-22, S-23; only general king safety) or the UCI castling notation (S-25). R-1 declares "The input contract is valid orthodox FEN" as an ordinary requirement line, yet the product (after its fix pass) rejects malformed FEN with an "Invalid FEN:" Error; that behaviour lives in README/fix.md, not the spec. R-4 decides "no additional draw statuses" without marking it as the builder's choice (consistent with the request). No contradictions with the request found.
tests_notes: TC-8 measures middlegame and depth-2 timing in one test with a single cold measurement each. TC-5 mixes promotion generation with general illegal-UCI rejection; TC-3 and TC-4 IDs are each used by two tests. TC-9 is tied to message wording (/^Invalid FEN/) and to the FEN error not being IllegalMoveError, so another correct build that throws TypeError or a differently worded Error, or IllegalMoveError for bad FEN (all acceptable per the inventory), would fail it. TC-6 asserts the exact reply list for its check position and TC-1 the exact start list, which is fine for any correct build. The suite catches removal of the IllegalMoveError export only incidentally (instanceof undefined in TC-9); assert.throws(fn, IllegalMoveError) silently accepts any error if the export is missing.
maintainer: The 0x88 board uses bare numeric indices throughout (castling homes 4/116, rook corners 0/7/112/119, en-passant ranks 2/5) and boardAfter is shared between legality filtering, castling transit checks and move application, so a change to move representation ripples through all three. Castling legality is split between addCastles (start and transit squares) and the generic king-safety filter (destination), which is easy to break when editing one without the other.
